job.style: a short story with Indian characters in everyday life

passage: Rohan and his grandfather sat on their porch in Rajasthan, watching the monsoon clouds gather. 'It is so hot today, Grandpa,' Rohan said, 'does this heat mean the climate is changing?' His grandfather smiled, 'No, Rohan. Weather is what happens outside right now, like today's heat or rain. Climate is the average pattern of weather over many, many years.' He pointed to the fields. 'Some people think global warming is just a future problem, but we see it now through erratic monsoons and intense heatwaves affecting our crops. It is not just about rising temperatures; our rainfall patterns are shifting too. People often blame only big factories for greenhouse gases, but our daily choices, like wasting electricity or using plastic, also add to the problem. Some worry that the greenhouse effect is entirely bad, but it actually keeps Earth warm enough for life. The real danger is the enhanced greenhouse effect, where extra gases trap too much heat. Even if we have a cold winter day, it does not mean the planet is cooling. The long-term trend shows the Earth is steadily warming, causing glaciers to melt and sea levels to rise, partly because warmer water takes up more space than cold water.'

items.evidence: Climate is the average pattern of weather over many, many years.
items.q: Rohan wants to know what Rajasthan's climate is like. What should he study?
options: Weather records from many, many years
The weather of this monsoon season
Today's heat and rain outside his house
How the weather changes from day to day
items.explain: Climate is the average pattern of weather over many years, so one day or one season is not enough.

wrong.why: thinks climate is just the weather of the present season
mixes up weather (right now) with climate
thinks climate is about day-to-day weather changes

items.evidence: Some people think global warming is just a future problem, but we see it now through erratic monsoons and intense heatwaves affecting our crops.
items.q: Rohan's friend says global warming will only matter when they grow up. What would Grandpa reply?
options: It is already here, in erratic monsoons
He is right, it has not started yet
It matters only if every day feels hotter
It means hotter days, but rain stays the same
items.explain: Grandpa says we already see global warming now, through erratic monsoons and intense heatwaves hurting crops.

wrong.why: thinks climate change is only a future problem
expects warming to make every day hotter
misses that rainfall patterns are shifting too

items.evidence: People often blame only big factories for greenhouse gases, but our daily choices, like wasting electricity or using plastic, also add to the problem.
items.q: Rohan leaves the fan running in an empty room every day. How does this affect greenhouse gases?
options: It adds to them by wasting electricity
It has no effect, as only factories add them
It cools the room, so it cools the Earth
It hardly matters, as these gases are tiny
items.explain: Daily choices like wasting electricity also add greenhouse gases, not just big factories.

wrong.why: thinks only factories and cars add these gases
confuses cooling a room with cooling the planet
thinks small amounts of gas do not matter

items.evidence: Some worry that the greenhouse effect is entirely bad, but it actually keeps Earth warm enough for life.
items.q: What would most likely happen to Earth if there were no greenhouse effect at all?
options: Earth would be too cold for life
Earth would be safer and healthier for life
More sunlight would get in, making Earth hotter
The ozone hole would close and stop warming
items.explain: The greenhouse effect keeps Earth warm enough for life; without it, Earth would be too cold.

wrong.why: thinks the greenhouse effect is always harmful
thinks greenhouse gases block the Sun's rays
links global warming to the ozone hole

items.evidence: Even if we have a cold winter day, it does not mean the planet is cooling.
items.q: Delhi has its coldest winter day in many years. What does this tell us about global warming?
options: One cold day does not change the long-term trend
It proves the planet has started cooling
The climate changed overnight from hot to cold
Warming is false, as every day should feel hotter
items.explain: A cold winter day does not mean the planet is cooling; the long-term trend still shows steady warming.

wrong.why: thinks a cold day disproves global warming
thinks climate change means day-to-day weather change
expects warming to make every day hotter
